en.name: Eucharistic Miracle of Ferrara
en.summary: During an Easter Mass in 1171, a broken host reportedly bled visibly enough to spatter the church vault above the altar.
en.body: According to the tradition recorded in Ferrara, Italy, during the Easter Mass of 1171 the celebrant broke the consecrated host as part of the usual rite, and it reportedly began to bleed so profusely that droplets spattered onto the vaulted ceiling above the altar, marks that were said to remain visible for a considerable time afterward. News of the event spread quickly through the region, and the local community began construction of a new church, the Basilica of Santa Maria in Vado, specifically to enshrine and commemorate the site of the reported miracle. The basilica, expanded and rebuilt over subsequent centuries, remains a significant place of Eucharistic devotion in Ferrara today, with a chapel preserving the tradition of the event.
